S2.title: Universal Credit
S2.retrieval_query: What did the UK government's official guidance and Treasury announcements state about the Job Support Scheme and Universal Credit for employees unable to work in tier 3 areas?

passages.P4: Universal Credit is a payment to help with your living costs. It’s paid monthly - or twice a month for some people in Scotland.
passages.P5: You may be able to get it if you’re on a low income, out of work or you cannot work.
passages.P6: This guide is also available in Welsh (Cymraeg) and in an easy read format.
passages.P7: If you live in Northern Ireland, go to Universal Credit in Northern Ireland.
passages.P9: Sign in to your Universal Credit account if you already have one.
passages.P10: ## If you already get other benefits
passages.P11: Universal Credit is replacing Housing Benefit and income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA).
passages.P12: If you’re getting these benefits, you do not need to do anything unless either:
passages.P13:
* your circumstances change
* you get a letter called a ‘Migration Notice’ telling you that you must claim Universal Credit
passages.P14: If you get a Migration Notice, you must move to Universal Credit by the deadline date in your letter to keep getting financial support.
passages.P15: You’ll stop getting these benefits when you or your partner claim Universal Credit. If you or your partner gets Pension Credit, this will also stop if one of you claims Universal Credit.
passages.P16: You’ll continue getting any other benefits you already receive, such as Personal Independence Payment (PIP) or Carer’s Allowance.
passages.P17: If you get certain other benefits at the same time as Universal Credit, the amount of Universal Credit you receive will be reduced.
